messages:
mira: paging: infra-bot just fired an alert for >50% retransmit on IB fabric to serving cluster A :pager:. seeing client timeouts and a cascade of container restarts on rack-12 nodes. root ts 3766123456

infra-bot: ALERT: IB_RETRANSMIT_RATE_HIGH cluster=serve-prod-A threshold=0.5 current=0.62

jon: oncall here. confirming, dashboard shows sustained TX drops and a spike in recv stalls. some pods reported CUDA OOM during heavy retry bursts.

linda: which regions affected? any customer-facing latency increase?

mira: traffic reports show 18% tail latency increase for embeddings endpoints in eu-west. several dedicated instances lost kvcache connection then died (OOM). early signs point to ECMP path split causing out-of-order packets + retransmit amplification.

sam: copying logs from one node (rack-12-3):
```
[2026-03-15T02:07:13Z] ibx: retransmit=0.58 drop=0.02
[2026-03-15T02:07:15Z] runtime: cuda oom: alloc 4.2GB failed in attention kernel
[2026-03-15T02:07:15Z] containerd: restarting container serving-runtime-xyz (exit code 137)
```

jon: nice, so heavy retransmit -> recv stalls -> kvcache miss storm -> memory spike during recomputation -> OOMs. chain reaction. we need a mitigation plan before customers hit error budgets.

mira: mitigation plan candidate: (1) route eu-west production serving traffic to eu-central fallback pool with degraded model variant, (2) enable per-pod rate-limiter to throttle prefixes to reduce retry amplification, (3) cordon & drain the worst nodes in rack-12 to stop noisy restarts, (4) infra escalate to networking to isolate switch.

linda: +1 on fallback routing. can we do automated fallback via smart-routing policy or is manual?

jon: we can flip routing policy to prefer region preference -> eu-central, will take ~2 min to converge. I'll run the canary shift 10% -> 30% -> 100%. mira, want me to start now?

mira: start now. set canary to 10% then watch tail latencies and failed token rates. label this incident SEV2 for customers (no full outage yet).

pagerduty-bot: NOTE: PagerDuty incident created: PD-48921 assigned to oncall (jon). Severity: SEV2.

sam: infra note: i've opened ticket to networking (net-team) and provided flow logs + failed port IDs: switch sw-r12-07, ports 13-16 show high discards. pinging net oncall @lina-net.

linda: while routing changes happen, push a temporary runtime config to reduce batch_size from 256 -> 96 and reduce prefetch concurrency. that should lower memory working set and reduce OOM probability. who will deploy?

jon: i'll push the runtime config via rollout API. command: `POST /internal/rollout` body: `{ "target": "serve-prod-A", "batch_size": 96, "concurrency_limit": 2 }`

mira: tagging it in the thread. jon, after 10% canary check, bump to 30% if successful. monitor container restart rate and CUDA OOM logs.

sam: net-team replied: "observed ECMP path split between spine-3 and spine-4 causing out-of-order delivery; applying flow pinning to ports on sw-r12-07 to stabilize." they will apply change in 5 min and report back.

infra-bot: ACTION: applied route preference change for serve-prod-A canary=10% -> eu-central fallback pool.

jon: canary has 10% traffic shifted. early metrics: eu-central tail latency +5%, failed token rate stable. rack-12 restart rate decreased by ~30% after batch change. no new OOM lines in last 60s on canary nodes.

linda: good. continue 10 -> 30 -> 100 as long as no regression in failures. also add temporary alert for container restart rate > 3/min to catch regressions.

mira: net-team: confirm when flow pinning is applied. sam, please coordinate to validate packet reorder metrics after change.

sam: net-team reports change applied at 02:12Z. reordering metric dropped from p99=12ms to p99=2.1ms. looks promising.

jon: bumping canary to 30% now. watching.

infra-bot: ROLLOUT: canary=30% at 02:15Z.

mira: monitoring: eu-west remaining pool still showing some restarts but overall error rate trending down. linda, keep the batch limit in place for 30 mins minimum, then we can slowly raise if stable.

linda: will do. I've also opened a followup PR to adjust default batch heuristics to be more conservative for transient network error patterns. link: https://git.redwood/pr/serve/batch-guardrails 

pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: PD-48921 status: mitigated -> partial. next: postmortem & Cx comms. assign to mira+jon for RCA.

mira: thanks team. next steps: (1) keep routing and reduced batch in place for 30m, (2) schedule scheduled maintenance window with net-team to test spine redundancy and ECMP configs, (3) start an incident timeline doc and collect logs. I'll draft a status update for impacted customers (eu-west embeddings).

jon: agree. handing back to SRE monitoring rotation at 02:45Z. I'll add notes in incident doc.

mira: handing to linda for follow-through and postmortem. linda, over to you. :white_check_mark:

linda: taking over. I'll coordinate postmortem and customer comms. closing out active on-call tasks now.

sam: thanks all — net-team to followup with root cause analysis on ECMP split and any hardware fixes.

mira: incident thread closed for active mitigation. leave open for postmortem collection.

jon: last message: observed total customer error budget consumption +0.7% during incident. will include in RCA.
